messages:
support: Heads-up: Tenant tenant-42 experiencing 5xx/gateway timeouts from hosted API since ~11:02 PDT. Customer on paid plan — SLA risk. Spikes line up with autoscale events.

mike: I'm taking this. Which endpoints and what traffic profile?

support: Mainly POST /v1/generate and chat streaming. Sustained burst ~120 rps for ~90s, then errors. First wave were 504s from gateway. Quick log snippet below.

support: ```
2026-03-16T18:02:11Z gateway: upstream timeout to inference-proxy(10.3.2.12):504
2026-03-16T18:02:12Z hpa-controller: scale up triggered for pool-tenant-42 x3->x15
2026-03-16T18:02:14Z keda: ScaledObject trigger: queueLength=98
2026-03-16T18:02:17Z inference: model init start
2026-03-16T18:02:45Z inference: model init complete
2026-03-16T18:03:05Z gateway: upstream closed connection
```

ashley: That model-init gap (~28s) is too long for our gateway timeout. Looks like pods are doing cold model loads on scale-up. Do we have prewarm configured?

mike: Can you run and paste `kubectl get hpa,pods,scaledobject -l tenant=tenant-42 -n inference -o wide` and the slow pod logs? Need to confirm minReplicaCount and cooldown settings.

support: Pasting current state: 

support: ```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME                          SCALETARGETREF   MINPODS   MAXPODS   CURRENT
pool-tenant-42-hpa            Deployment/pool   1         20        3

$ kubectl get scaledobject -n inference
NAME                         COOLDOWN   MINREPLICACOUNT
pool-tenant-42-scaledobj     300        1
```

support: Logs (slow pod):

support: ```
[2026-03-16T18:02:17Z] model fetch start: downloading weights (13.1s)
[2026-03-16T18:02:30Z] weights write complete
[2026-03-16T18:02:30Z] quantize step: 11.6s
[2026-03-16T18:02:41Z] init runtime: 3.1s
[2026-03-16T18:02:45Z] model ready
```

support: So fetch+quant+init ~= 28s. Gateway timeout default is 25s for upstream.

chao: With minReplicaCount=1 we only keep one warm pod. A tenant burst starting from 1->15 will produce many new pods that do full model init. We should either increase minReplicaCount for heavy models / tenants or use prewarm pool.

oncall-bot: @pagerduty incident created: INC-20260316-47 — tenant-42 scaling delays causing 5xx/gateway timeouts. Escalation to SRE rotation.

mike: Immediate mitigations to reduce customer 5xxs:
1) bump ScaledObject minReplicaCount to 3 for this tenant (reduces cold starts)
2) temporarily route tenant traffic to dedicated warm pool if available (switch routing var)
3) consider increasing gateway upstream timeout to 35s for tenant routing while we stabilize (tradeoff: client wait)
4) longer-term: add model init time metric and prewarm config on tenant onboarding

ashley: Also spotted an auth token rotate event earlier at 10:58 that produced a handful of 401 retries — could have spiked background control-plane calls and increased queue length. Verify auth service logs around 10:55-11:05.

support: Customer asked for a quick fix — willing to accept temporary cost increase. Requesting SRE change now.

mike: Applying patch: `kubectl patch scaledobject pool-tenant-42-scaledobj -n inference --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":3}}'`

mike: Patch applied. Observing metrics: pod count increased to 4 (1 extra warm + 3 new), model init tail decreased. Gateway 5xx count is trending down. :thumbsup: 

ashley: Note: lowering KEDA cooldown to 60s may make it faster to scale-down/scale-up in short bursts, but risks oscillation. We'll keep cooldown at 300s for now.

chao: Follow-ups:
- Add prewarm flag to tenant onboarding for models with init>10s.
- Add alert that fires when scale-up leads to >X% of requests routed to pods younger than 30s.
- Document playbook: check ScaledObject.minReplicaCount, model init time, and recently rotated tokens.

support: Customer updated and appreciated quick action. Monitoring for 24h; will close if stable.

mike: Postmortem TODO: correlate billing/auth throttles, scale-up timing, and consider autoscaler policy that maintains a small buffer above min for heavy tenants.

support: Thanks everyone.
